content.tagline: Korean skincare built to show a result in a single use
content.descriptor: MAOOM is the own brand of the Seoul studio SkinRoom: a NAD-based Skin Boosting line, a mask with a visible effect in fifteen minutes, an overnight peel and a thermal serum. Six items are notified in the European CPNP register.
about: MAOOM is the brand of SkinRoom Co., Ltd. of Seoul, Gangdong district. The company calls its approach "It's not Skincare. It's Futurecare" and builds it around a single idea: the result should be visible at once, not after a month of use.

That is where the formats come from. The ReFit mask is stated to give visible lifting in fifteen minutes, the glAHAssy 3 cream works as exfoliation during sleep, and the Therma V serum is built around thermal care and NAD plumping. These are not variations on one base but different mechanics for different jobs.

The core of the range is the three Skin Boosting items: a toner, a serum and a cream. The company builds them on its own Skin Liposomal NAD+ complex and, by its account, on a dual-layer thermal dispersion — both stated as in-house developments.

Six items of the brand are notified in CPNP, the European portal for cosmetic product notification, all notifications dated 27 July 2026. The company states shipments to markets in Asia, North America and Europe.

lines.name: Skin Boosting — the NAD-based core line
lines.note: Three items: a toner 150 ml, a serum 50 ml and a cream 50 ml. The company describes them as one routine, where the toner sets the first step, the serum works on skin density and the cream closes with moisture and glow. The component stated across the line is the Skin Liposomal NAD+ complex.

lines.name: Therma V Serum, 20 ml
lines.note: A thermal-care serum. The company places it in the skin-booster format and describes it through a combination of thermal action and NAD plumping. It is the smallest volume in the range: the item is presented as a concentrate rather than as everyday care.

lines.name: ReFit Mask, 100 ml
lines.note: A mask with a stated visible lifting effect in fifteen minutes. The format is built for a single result before an event rather than for a course, and that is a rare argument on a retail shelf: the buyer verifies the claim the same evening.

lines.name: glAHAssy 3 Cream, 50 ml
lines.note: An overnight cream with an exfoliating action. The company reports that clinical trials on acne have been completed for this item. Its niche is the buyer who wants a peel without daytime restrictions.

lines.name: Perfect Radiance Cushion, main unit and refill
lines.note: The only make-up item in the range, supplied as a set with a refill. The company describes it as smooth on the outside and moist inside. This item is not part of the CPNP set.

tech.name: Skin Liposomal NAD+ complex
tech.note: An in-house development, as stated by the company. NAD+ is a coenzyme around which a whole direction in skincare has formed in recent years; the liposomal form is stated as the delivery method. We present this as the company's description: no trial protocols were provided to us.

tech.name: Dual-layer thermal dispersion
tech.note: The second stated in-house mechanism, underlying the Therma V Serum. The company describes it as thermal care producing an effect of plumped skin.

tech.name: A result in a single use
tech.note: A deliberate design principle rather than a marketing line: the fifteen-minute mask, the overnight peel and the thermal serum are all built for it. The company names this directly as its difference from cumulative-action skincare.

tech.name: Clinical trials on acne
tech.note: Stated by the company for the glAHAssy 3 Cream. We hold no trial reports, so we pass this on as a manufacturer's statement rather than a fact verified by us.

tech.name: CPNP notification
tech.note: Six items of the brand have been notified in the European CPNP portal, all documents dated 27 July 2026. The notification files were provided to us by the company on 4 September 2026.

content.exportNote: The company states shipments to markets in Asia, North America and Europe and confirms international delivery on its own storefront. Six items are notified in CPNP, which removes part of the entry barrier into the European Union. Latin America is not covered by the company — that is the direction this profile was built for.
